The study is anchored on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Task–Technology Fit (TTF), Information Systems Success Model (ISSM), and Records Management Life Cycle (RMLC). These theories provide the foundation for understanding user acceptance of the system, the alignment of the technology with salon operational tasks, the evaluation of system effectiveness and quality, and the proper management of appointment records throughout their lifecycle. Together, these theoretical foundations support the development of a system that is user-friendly, useful, operationally efficient, secure, and capable of maintaining reliable appointment and service records for Kaye’s Hair Salon and Spa.

The Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), developed by Davis (1989), explains user acceptance of technology through two major factors: perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use. In the context of the Web-Based Appointment System for Kaye’s Hair Salon and Spa, TAM is applicable because customers, managers, and admins are more likely to accept and use the platform when they find it helpful in improving appointment scheduling and simple to operate.

The system supports perceived usefulness by allowing customers to book appointments online, select one or more services, check available time slots, choose payment options, and receive appointment receipts without relying on manual booking methods. It also benefits managers and admins by making appointment monitoring, payment verification, schedule control, and service management more organized and efficient. At the same time, the system supports perceived ease of use through a clear and user-friendly interface that simplifies the booking process, OTP-based appointment management, payment submission, and receipt generation. Features such as accessible service selection, visible schedule availability, and guided transaction steps help users complete tasks with less difficulty. Overall, TAM supports the study by explaining that the proposed system is more likely to be accepted and continuously used when users perceive it as useful, convenient, and easy to navigate.

The Task–Technology Fit (TTF) model, developed by Goodhue and Thompson (1995), emphasizes that an information system improves user performance when its features match the tasks that users must accomplish. This model is applicable because salon operations involve specific scheduling and management tasks that require structured tools. Core tasks include monitoring appointment schedules, avoiding time conflicts, managing services, monitoring appointment progress, and maintaining appointment history and records. The salon appointment system provides corresponding technology capabilities such as availability checking, appointment lifecycle management, role-based access, dashboard monitoring, and record generation. When the technology fits these tasks, managers and admins can perform operational work more accurately and efficiently, while customers experience a more reliable and convenient booking process. TTF
strengthens the framework by directly connecting the system’s modules to real salon activities, supporting functional relevance and operational value.
The Information Systems Success Model (ISSM), developed by

and McLean (1992), provides a structured approach for evaluating whether an information system is successful. This model is suitable for the salon appointment system because success is measured not only by system availability but also by the quality of the system, the quality of information produced, user satisfaction, and operational benefits. System quality includes reliability, security, speed, and user-friendliness, all of which are necessary for smooth booking and monitoring. Information quality covers accuracy and completeness, ensuring that available slots, appointment schedules, service details, and status updates remain correct and consistent across users. Service quality refers to the support provided to users through clear prompts, guidance, and administrative maintenance to ensure stable operations. The model also considers use or intention to use and user satisfaction, reflecting consistent adoption by customers, managers, and admins and a positive experience during transactions. Lastly, net benefits reflect outcomes such as reduced booking conflicts, improved schedule visibility, improved monitoring, better record organization, and enhanced customer convenience. ISSM supports the study by establishing measurable indicators of system performance and impact.
The Records Management Life Cycle (RMLC), developed by Theodore
(1960), provides a structured approach to managing records from creation to final disposition. This concept is essential to the salon appointment system because the platform functions not only as a

booking tool but also as a record-keeping system that stores appointment history, customer booking details, service information, and operational summaries. The lifecycle approach supports proper record creation when appointments are booked and accounts are registered, record use when customers, managers, and admins view schedules and status updates, record maintenance when appointments are confirmed, rescheduled, canceled, or completed, and record retention when appointment histories are stored for monitoring and reporting purposes. The framework also guides the proper disposition or archiving of older records based on salon policy, helping ensure organized storage and controlled data growth. The conceptual framework of the study is based on the Input–Process–Output (IPO) model, which presents the flow of activities involved in the development of the proposed Web-Based Appointment System for Kaye’s Hair Salon and Spa. Under the input stage, the study includes data gathering, theories related to the system, and interpretation of data. Data gathering provides the necessary information about the existing appointment practices, user needs, and operational problems of the salon. Theories related to the system serve as the foundation for understanding system acceptance, task alignment, system success, and records management. Interpretation of data allows the researchers to analyze the collected information and use it as a basis for identifying system requirements and project direction.

In the process stage, the study undergoes analysis, system design, implementation, deployment, and maintenance. Analysis involves examining the gathered data and identifying the problems and requirements of the salon. System design focuses on planning the structure, features, database, and interface of the proposed platform. Implementation refers to the actual development of the system using the selected technologies and tools. Deployment covers the installation and release of the system for actual use, while maintenance ensures that the system remains functional, updated, and responsive to needed improvements after implementation.

In the output stage, the result of these inputs and processes is the development of the Web-Based Appointment System for Kaye’s Hair Salon and Spa. The system is expected to provide a more organized, efficient, and reliable way of handling salon appointments, service management, and operational monitoring. Through this framework, the study shows how relevant information, theoretical support, and systematic development procedures contribute to the successful creation of the proposed system.

The organizational structure of Kaye’s Hair Salon and Spa is composed of three main levels: the Admin/Owner, Manager, and Staff. The Admin/Owner serves as the highest authority and is responsible for overseeing the overall business operations, managing system access, monitoring reports, and making major decisions for the salon. The Manager assists the owner by supervising daily salon activities, monitoring appointments, managing customer transactions, and ensuring that services are properly handled. The Staff are responsible for providing salon services, assisting customers, and supporting the daily operations of the salon. This structure shows a clear flow of authority and responsibility, helping the salon maintain organized management and smooth service delivery.

Fishbone Diagram presents the major causes affecting the appointment scheduling and management process of Kaye’s Hair Salon and Spa. It shows that the existing manual process may lead to problems caused by people, process/method, records/data, communication, schedule/availability, and technology/system. The programming environment used in the development of the Web-based Appointment System for Kaye’s Hair Salon and Spa consisted of a combination of frontend, backend, database, and development tools that supported the creation, testing, and deployment of the system. These technologies were selected to ensure that the system would be responsive, secure, maintainable, and capable of handling the required functions for customers, managers, and the admin/owner.
This section discusses the technologies used in developing the web front end of the proposed system.

React.js serves as the primary architectural framework for the system’s user interface. Developed as a declarative and component-based JavaScript library, React.js allowed the researchers to build a sophisticated Single Page Application (SPA). In this system, React.js manages the complex state of the appointment booking process, ensuring that service selections, and time slots are updated instantaneously. By utilizing a virtual Document Object Model (DOM), React.js optimizes rendering performance, providing customers with a fluid and seamless experience that mimics a native desktop application.

Tailwind CSS was used to design the user interface of the system. It is a utility-first CSS framework that allowed the researchers to create a responsive, clean, and visually consistent layout. Tailwind CSS was especially useful in making the system adaptable to different screen sizes, including mobile devices, tablets, and desktop computers.
This section discusses the programming languages and frameworks used in developing the web back end of the proposed system.

is the robust PHP framework utilized to develop the server-side logic and API of the system. It was chosen for its advanced features, such as the Eloquent Object-Relational Mapper (ORM), which simplifies database interactions, and its built-in security protocols including CSRF protection and encrypted session management. Within the context of the salon system,

acts as the central coordinator—processing booking requests, calculating 10% mandatory deposits, and managing role-based access for Admins and Managers. Its modular structure ensures that the backend remains organized and easily maintainable as the salon's requirements evolve.
JavaScript is the fundamental programming language used to implement the system’s dynamic behavior. On the client side, JavaScript facilitates asynchronous communication with the

backend, allowing users to submit forms, verify OTPs (One-Time Passwords), and upload payment receipts without the need for traditional page refreshes. Its versatility enables the researchers to create highly interactive elements, such as real-time search filters for services and
automated calculation of remaining balances, significantly improving the overall responsiveness and usability of the platform.
PHP (Hypertext Preprocessor) is the core server-side scripting language that powers the

framework. It is responsible for executing the business logic of the salon system on the server. PHP handles the heavy lifting of the application, such as processing payment logic, communicating with the MySQL database, and generating automated email notifications for confirmed or rescheduled appointments. Its deep integration with various web servers and its ability to handle complex data structures make it an indispensable variable in the system's backend development.

MySQL is the relational database management system used to store and organize the salon's critical information. It manages structured data across multiple tables, including users, appointments, services, and payments. For Kaye's Hair Salon and Spa, MySQL ensures data integrity and consistency, allowing for reliable tracking of customer booking histories and financial records. The researchers utilized MySQL’s indexing capabilities to ensure that even as the database grows, queries for available time slots and daily sales reports remain efficient and high-performing.

This section presents the implementation results of the developed Web-Based Appointment System for Kaye’s Hair Salon and Spa, focusing on the testing activities and survey evaluation conducted after development. The system was tested based on its major functions, including appointment booking, email-based OTP verification, service selection, schedule checking, payment handling, receipt generation, ratings and feedback, role-based access, notifications, and reports. The system was developed using
for the backend, React for the frontend, and MySQL for the database, supporting centralized records and web-based access for customers, admin, and manager.

Unit testing was conducted to check each system module individually before connecting it to the full workflow. The tested modules included customer email verification, appointment booking, service selection, date and time selection, payment process, receipt generation, customer dashboard, rescheduling, ratings and feedback, admin login, manager login, service management, customer management, holiday management, payment account management, and reports. This testing confirmed that the major functions were able to perform their intended tasks before proceeding to integration.
Integration testing focused on verifying whether the system components worked together properly. The interaction between the React interface,

backend, MySQL database, and email service was checked through major user transactions such as booking an appointment, sending and verifying OTP, selecting services, choosing payment options, uploading proof of payment, generating receipts, updating appointment status, and displaying reports. The results showed that the system components were able to exchange and update information correctly across customer, admin, and manager modules.

Compatibility testing was conducted to determine whether the system could function across common devices and browsers. Since the system is web-based, it was tested using desktops, laptops, tablets, and smartphones through browsers such as Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari. The testing confirmed that customers could access the booking pages, verify email OTP, upload payment proof, view receipts, and manage appointments, while the admin and manager could access their dashboards and monitoring pages. This supports the system’s objective of providing accessible appointment services through internet-enabled devices.

Performance testing measured the system’s ability to respond efficiently during normal use. Functions such as loading services, checking schedules, processing bookings, sending OTP, uploading payment proof, generating receipts, filtering appointment records, and viewing dashboard summaries were observed. The survey results also supported this finding, as the end
users rated Performance Efficiency with an overall mean of 3.80, interpreted as Very Efficient, while the IT experts rated it 3.60, also interpreted as Very Efficient.

Load testing was conducted to observe how the system performed when multiple records and repeated user actions were processed. The testing included scenarios such as customers viewing services, booking appointments, checking schedules, submitting payment details, and accessing appointment records. On the management side, appointment records, customer records, services, ratings, holidays, and reports were reviewed while system transactions were being processed. The system remained stable under expected salon usage and was able to support the daily operations required by the salon.

This section presents the evaluation results of the Web-Based Appointment System for Kaye’s Hair Salon and Spa based on the responses of two groups of respondents: twenty (20) end users composed of fifteen (15) customers and five (5) salon management personnel, and ten (10) IT experts. The questionnaire for the end users focused on the ISO/IEC 25010 software quality characteristics of functional suitability, performance efficiency, and usability, while the questionnaire for the IT experts covered functional suitability, performance efficiency, compatibility, usability, reliability, security, maintainability, and portability. The weighted mean and verbal interpretation were used to determine the level of acceptability and quality of the developed system.

summarizes the evaluation of the system by the end users. Performance Efficiency obtained the highest overall mean of 3.80, which shows that the system was viewed as fast and efficient during use. Usability received the lowest overall mean of 3.66, but it still falls within the highest interpretation range. The general mean of 3.73 indicates that the system was highly acceptable to the end users.
